question: Refer to the exhibit. Two data center fabrics use vPC data center interconnect. The system MAC value on SW1 is 00:23:04:ee:be:20. Which value must be set to configure the system MAC address on SW3?
context: Topology: VPC 20 domain with SW4/SW3 on top and SW2/SW1 on bottom, cross-connected via PO 100.
imageNote: Diagram: VPC 20 domain with SW4/SW3 on top and SW2/SW1 on bottom, cross-connected to each other via PO 100.
theory: Within a single vPC domain, both peer switches share one virtual system MAC address derived from the vPC domain ID, which is why SW1 and SW2, forming one domain, share the same value. When two separate vPC domains are interconnected back-to-back, as with SW3/SW4 forming a second domain toward SW1/SW2, each domain must use a distinct vPC domain ID so its derived virtual system MAC differs from the other domain's — reusing the same MAC across both domains would create address duplication and break the loop-prevention and forwarding logic vPC relies on to distinguish peer devices. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 2 — vPC Domain ID and System MAC in Back-to-Back vPC Designs)
